ops.title: cmd.py flat-walk reconcile introduced 7 fail-open holes — fail-closed principle
ops.body: 2026-07-19 adversarial review (fable finder+refuter) of the reconciled evt.cmd API caught a critical regression BEFORE landing: collapsing the recursive sh -c/eval descent into a flat self.line.occurrences walk (banking on cc-transcript 14.7 payload-parts) silently dropped nested-payload rm detection wherever the parser can't statically resolve a construct. bash -c "rm -rf $HOME" → calls('rm')==[] (was BLOCKED pre-reconcile). 7 holes: (1/3) tainted double-quoted shell payload not descended; (2) process substitution <(rm -rf /) produces no occurrence; (4) brace expansion rm {/,tmp/x} verified=True (glob.has_magic ignores braces); (5) xargs stripped as transparent wrapper → zero targets vacuously verified (stdin operands invisible); (6) arithmetic $((..)) dropped, complete stays True. UNIFYING PRINCIPLE for cmd.py: the parser's occurrence enumeration is NOT complete — fail CLOSED on anything not statically resolvable (surface via re-parse where feasible, else complete=False/verified=False). Never return verified=True over partial/zero targets. Fix in flight on cmd-api branch.
